shows.name: LP News
shows.description: AI and tech news briefings, made for Luke with Muse.

shows.name: LP Learning
shows.description: AI explainers, how-tos, tech history and short fiction, made for Luke with Muse.

episodes.title: The Notary's Stamp
episodes.description: A certificate authority's private keys were exposed for months and what to do about it. Plus Anthropic's $80B "loss" (mostly an accounting charge), Mistral's new voice stack, why AI keeps citing fake statistics, and a Google Cloud power fault in London.

episodes.title: Suitcase for SuiteWorld
episodes.description: What to expect at your first SuiteWorld - what people wear, what a day actually looks like, and the things worth making sure you do before Wednesday.

episodes.title: Space Bunny Confesses
episodes.description: The mystery "Space Bunny" model turns out to be MiniMax's new cheap model. Plus Mistral's tiny forecasting models, Amazon's cash-flow-negative AI bet, and a TV debloat tool.

episodes.title: One Key, One Purpose
episodes.description: OpenCode's breach and how to protect your API keys, OpenAI's newest rogue-AI incident reports, sites closing doors to AI agents, a Namecheap domain suspension, and Linux 7.2's AI-assisted commits.

episodes.title: Better, Faster, Same Price
episodes.description: DeepSeek ships a stronger model at the same price, Lean gets verified kernels, and Let's Encrypt shrinks certificates to 64 days. Plus Tencent's memory model and a tool for estimating local AI speed.

episodes.title: Your Cloudflare Cabinet: The Four Things Worth Knowing
episodes.description: Decoding the Cloudflare dashboard you clicked through: accounts, members, zones, the four settings worth knowing, and a four-step checklist that changes nothing.

episodes.title: Who Answers When Someone Types Your Domain
episodes.description: A jargon-free walk through what a domain name is, how DNS works like the contacts app on your phone, and what it meant when you changed your nameservers to Cloudflare.

episodes.title: Twelve Testers and a Signing Key
episodes.description: Everything it takes to get a vibe-coded app onto Google Play in 2026, from the $25 developer account and the twelve-tester closed test to app bundles, signing keys, and the PWA shortcut. Plus a newer free option for sharing apps with just friends and family.

episodes.title: Your Domain Is a Ledger: DNS and Cloudflare, Finally Explained
episodes.description: What Cloudflare actually is, what happened when the setup wizard had you make an account, a team, and nameserver changes, and which parts of your dashboard matter versus which you can safely ignore. DNS records, proxying, free SSL, Pages, Workers, and R2, in plain English with a little ledger humor.

episodes.title: Just Timestamps
episodes.description: Anthropic's model solves the 25-year-old NIST ECDSA seed mystery, a critical GitLab emergency patch, FLUX 3 Klein open weights, Mercor's map of what AI benchmarks miss, and Google Play's private vibe-coded apps.

episodes.title: Git, GitHub, and the Undo Button
episodes.description: What GitHub actually is and how people use it, from commits and branches to pull requests, Actions and Pages, plus where AI coding tools fit.

episodes.title: Open Models, Real Limits
Tech Briefing October 15: Original Audio
Tech Briefing October 15: Specs, Scion, Lawsuits, Apertus, TSMC, and AI Music Labels
episodes.description: Maya and Devon on October 15 news - Figma Specs, Anthropic Scion, eight-state OpenAI lawsuits, Apertus 1.5, TSMC earnings, and YouTube Music AI labels - with builder takeaways.

episodes.title: Build It, Sell It: Cool Things to Make with AI and How They Pay
episodes.description: Maya and Devon on what you can actually build with AI — fun personal projects, tiny subscription tools, automation services, and digital products — plus the honest math on what each path pays.

episodes.title: Beyond the Chatbox: Dashboards, Decisions, and the Thousand-Agent Test
episodes.description: Maya and Devon on AI's shift from prose to verifiable outputs — Claude Dashboards with readable queries, OpenAI's Decisions API returning typed verdicts, and the thousand-agent bug hunt — with practical plays for NetSuite builders and auditors.

episodes.title: Your Own Private AI: The Local Model Playbook
episodes.description: Maya and Devon dig into running AI models on your own machine — Ollama, open weights, what fits on real hardware, this week's local AI news, and a privacy-first playbook for sensitive work.

episodes.title: The Real AI Fears: What's Actually Scary Right Now
episodes.description: Maya and Ben separate fact from hype on AI risks — cybercrime at scale, deepfakes, job displacement numbers, and the fears worth having.

episodes.title: Welcome to LP's Podcast
episodes.description: A quick hello from the new home of the AI in Practice series, short fiction, and tech histories.

episodes.title: Claude's Big Week: Haiku 5.5, Cheaper Caching, and the Agent Swarm
episodes.description: Maya and Devon break down Anthropic's huge early-October 2026 release wave — Haiku 5.5, halved cache pricing, Claude Code mods — plus the planner-executor-reviewer playbook and what a working builder should do differently on Monday.

episodes.title: Meet Muse: What Your Personal AI Agent Can Actually Do
episodes.description: A special episode all about Muse — Meta's personal AI agent. Maya and Devon tour what it can really do, what people use it for, what it costs, and how to get the most out of it.

episodes.title: The Pleasant Place
episodes.description: An original short story in the spirit of Steven L. Peck's A Short Stay in Hell. Tom Ellery wakes in an afterlife that seems... nice. Too nice. Narrated fiction.

episodes.title: How Computers Work
episodes.description: Maya and Ben trace the story of computing, from Jacquard's punched-card loom to the phone in your pocket.

episodes.title: Always-On Agents: Running Your Own Agent Team
episodes.description: Maya and Devon dig into the week's big shift: always-on coworker agents from Google, OpenAI, and Microsoft, plus the practical playbook for running your own team of agents — job descriptions, planner-executor-reviewer, and specialist tools like REA.
